description: Medium - Basic Concepts of SSL and Domains

questions.question: What three guarantees does HTTPS provide compared to HTTP?
options: Encryption, identity verification, and data integrity
Speed, reliability, and encryption
Anonymity, encryption, and performance
Identity verification, speed, and data compression
Encryption, anonymity, and server authentication

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describe what a browser checks when verifying an SSL certificate?
options: Whether the domain on the certificate matches the site being visited
Whether the certificate is within its validity period
Whether the certificate was issued by a trusted Certificate Authority
Whether the server is hosted on a recognised cloud provider
Whether the certificate covers all subdomains of the domain

questions.question: How does a Certificate Authority verify that you own a domain before issuing a certificate?
options: The CA checks WHOIS records to confirm the registrant's name matches the applicant
The CA sends a verification email to the domain's administrative contact
The CA asks you to add a specific TXT record to your DNS, then confirms it is there
The CA connects to your server and checks for a valid SSL certificate already installed
The CA requires a government-issued ID proving ownership of the domain

questions.question: What is the purpose of a CAA DNS record?
options: It maps your domain to an IP address for HTTPS traffic specifically
It specifies which Certificate Authorities are permitted to issue certificates for your domain
It redirects HTTP traffic to HTTPS automatically at the DNS level
It stores your SSL certificate so browsers can retrieve it directly
It verifies your domain ownership with Let's Encrypt during certificate issuance

questions.question: Which of the following are true about the TLS handshake?
options: It occurs before any application data is exchanged
It establishes the encrypted channel between browser and server
It typically adds one additional round-trip to the connection
It permanently replaces the need for DNS lookups on subsequent visits
It transfers the SSL certificate from browser to server for verification

questions.question: What is TLS termination and where does it typically occur?
options: The point where an SSL certificate expires and must be renewed
The process of revoking a compromised certificate at the CA level
The point where encrypted traffic becomes unencrypted, typically at a reverse proxy like nginx
The final step of the TLS handshake where encryption keys are destroyed
The process of converting HTTP traffic to HTTPS at the application level

questions.question: What is mixed content and why is it a problem?
options: When a site uses both DV and EV certificates simultaneously
When an HTTPS page loads resources such as images or scripts over HTTP
When a wildcard certificate covers both root and subdomain traffic
When HTTP and HTTPS traffic arrive on the same server port
When a self-signed certificate is used alongside a CA-signed certificate

questions.question: Which certificate types are correctly matched to their validation level?
options: DV — proves domain ownership only
OV — proves domain ownership and that the organisation exists
EV — deep background check on the organisation
DV — requires a government ID and physical address verification
EV — issued automatically and instantly like Let's Encrypt certificates

questions.question: What is the NET::ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID browser error most commonly caused by?
options: The certificate has passed its expiry date
The domain on the certificate does not match the site being visited
A self-signed certificate is being used on a production server
The server is running HTTP on port 443 instead of HTTPS
The CAA record is blocking the browser from trusting the certificate
